name: rule-label
description:
The rule-anchored label: tracked caps, an optional tabular index with its own dash, and a hairline that takes whatever width is left — the editorial device that turns a caption into furniture holding the column together.

This unit was DECLINED once, and the old note said why: the composite contract of that pass made every unit a container with `inline-size: 100%`, which would have forced the rule to always draw — on a centred head the label is meant to shrink to its content and let the rule collapse. That objection was about the contract, not the device. As a LEAF unit — no container, no forced width, exactly like `text` — the label keeps its content-driven size and the caller's layout still decides whether the rule appears. The declarations below are the ones the page carried; only the address changed.

base.$description: `inline-size: auto` is the point, not a default written out: the label sizes to its CONTENT, so on a centred head it shrinks and the rule collapses — the caller's layout decides whether the rule appears. That is the hugging class of the container contract, the exact non-container composite the old decline note said the contract lacked.

line.$description: The rule takes whatever width is left, which is what anchors the label to the column instead of leaving it floating over the content — and on a centred head, where the label shrinks to its content, it collapses to nothing on its own.

a11y.note: The hairline is `aria-hidden`: it is drawn, not said. The index reads as text because it is one — the counter variant increments it from DOM position, so what is announced matches what is shown.
